# Next day, new possibilities

So here I talked to anohter guy and apparently originally the service account svc_apache have only "GenericWrite" over the M3DC which makes as a good candidate to write any permission/attribute on that object.

Which consequently makes it possible to write the `msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity` so we can then proceed with RBCD attacks.

Now here what is Important to mentioning is that all the guides imply that we add a new fakepc so we can set a SPN, but in our case we have already a SPN(svc_apache) so techncally we can just perform the impersonation!

We need first to export the TGT ticket of svc_apache from the WEBAPP server via Ruberus.exe

![5e44191c47df17b83302502d77fc798f.png](../../../_resources/5e44191c47df17b83302502d77fc798f.png)

Next can we covert the ticker from kirbi to CCACHE and import in our session so we don't need the svc_apache creds and we can use `-k -no-pass`.

![2b541c252dc87e03e5fe10eca2391a26.png](../../../_resources/2b541c252dc87e03e5fe10eca2391a26.png)

And now we should be able to check the permisisons via rbdc.py.

EDIT: I was getting the wrong shell via meterpreter as I forgot to change the target of the exploit from Java to Windows(and adapt to a meterpreter Windows session).

![860db0f666b75ade2bcece4b48169d1e.png](../../../_resources/860db0f666b75ade2bcece4b48169d1e.png)

And now I can run all commands :D

![91748621b88f29d619192c491d4feb71.png](../../../_resources/91748621b88f29d619192c491d4feb71.png)

Now we can get the shell and try to elevate to NTSYSTEM via getsystem -t 6:

```
Background channel 3? [y/N]  y
meterpreter > getsystem -t 6
...got system via technique 6 (Named Pipe Impersonation (EFSRPC variant - AKA EfsPotato)).
meterpreter > getuid 
Server username: NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM
meterpreter >
```
